question: Should OpenClaw add a session-key pattern allowlist mode for `tools.sessions.visibility`, or fold this use case into the broader per-capability/per-agent session authorization design?
rationale: The request adds public config and changes which sessions and transcripts can cross isolation boundaries, so automation cannot safely choose the durable authorization model.

options.title: Design one consolidated model
options.body: Use this issue as the session-key allowlist input while reconciling it with the open per-capability, per-agent, sandbox, and A2A proposals before implementation.

options.title: Approve session-key allowlist
options.body: Accept `visibility="allowlist"` as its own config mode and require fail-closed matching plus list/history/send/status tests before merge.

options.title: Prefer broader scoping only
options.body: Decline a separate session-key allowlist and direct users to the eventual per-capability or per-agent authorization model.

recommendation.title: Design one consolidated model
recommendation.body: Use this issue as the session-key allowlist input while reconciling it with the open per-capability, per-agent, sandbox, and A2A proposals before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: Their history is strongest on the current shared session-tool authorization/config boundary.
